question: A 9-month-old infant is brought to casualty after a choking episode at home while eating a grape. He has complete airway obstruction — he is not making any sound, unable to cry or breathe, and is rapidly cyanosing. Which first-aid manoeuvre is correct for this infant?

answers.text: 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich manoeuvre) in an upright position

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Heimlich manoeuvre (abdominal thrusts) is CONTRAINDICATED in infants under 1 year of age. The infant's liver is large, relatively unprotected by the ribs, and prone to laceration with upward abdominal thrusts. Abdominal thrusts are used only for children ≥1 year (and adults).

answers.text: 5 back-blows followed by 5 chest thrusts, repeated in cycles

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For infants under 1 year with complete choking obstruction: 5 firm back-blows with the heel of the hand between the shoulder blades (infant face-down on the forearm), followed by 5 chest thrusts (two fingers on the sternum, one finger-breadth below the nipple line, delivered face-up). Cycles are repeated until the object is expelled or the infant becomes unconscious (then begin CPR). This is the BLS/ILCOR standard for infants.

answers.text: Immediate finger-sweep of the mouth to dislodge the object

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Blind finger-sweeps of the mouth are contraindicated — they can push the foreign body deeper and cause pharyngeal trauma. A finger sweep should only be performed if the object is CLEARLY VISIBLE in the mouth.

answers.text: 5 back-blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts, as for children over 1 year

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Abdominal thrusts are NOT used in infants under 1 year regardless of combination. For infants: back-blows + CHEST thrusts. For children ≥1 year: back-blows + abdominal thrusts (Heimlich). This age-based distinction is a critical safety rule.

overallFeedback.feedback: For infants <1 year: back-blows followed by CHEST thrusts. The Heimlich manoeuvre (abdominal thrusts) is contraindicated under 1 year because of liver injury risk. For children ≥1 year: back-blows + abdominal thrusts.
Correct. For infants <1 year with complete choking: 5 back-blows + 5 chest thrusts, repeated. Never use abdominal thrusts (Heimlich) in infants — risk of liver injury. Never blind finger-sweep.
